summary:
Earth Trace is an educational web platform designed to make space exploration more accessible and engaging through short, animated comics available in both English and Spanish.

I developed a bilingual website where users can explore different space missions, destinations, and historical achievements through illustrated stories. The platform provides an interactive reading experience and organizes content in an accessible and easy-to-understand format.

The project addresses the challenge of making scientific and technological information more engaging and understandable, especially for people who may find traditional educational materials difficult or uninteresting. By combining visual storytelling, animation, and bilingual content, Earth Trace transforms complex topics about space exploration into short and enjoyable learning experiences.

This project is important because it helps promote scientific curiosity, encourages learning about space exploration, and makes educational content accessible to a wider international audience. It also demonstrates how technology and creative storytelling can be combined to communicate scientific knowledge effectively.
details:
Earth Trace is a bilingual educational web platform that allows users to explore space exploration missions through short, illustrated comics in English and Spanish.

How it works:

The platform organizes stories by space destinations and missions. Users can browse the available stories, select a mission, and read it through a sequence of illustrated comic panels. Each story includes narration, dialogues, and captions displayed in the selected language. The content is structured using JSON files, making it easier to add new stories and translations.

Benefits and intended impact:

Earth Trace makes scientific information more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand. It encourages curiosity about astronomy, space exploration, and scientific achievements. Its bilingual approach also helps overcome language barriers and allows more people to access educational content. The intended impact is to promote informal science education, especially among young people and students.

Tools and technologies:

The project was developed using Astro as the web framework, JavaScript (ES modules), HTML, CSS, JSON, and SVG for generating the comic illustrations programmatically. Node.js and npm were used for development and dependency management. Playwright was also used for browser-based visual and interaction testing.

Creativity and innovation:

The creative aspect of Earth Trace is the combination of digital storytelling, comic illustrations, and scientific education. One important design decision was to separate the illustrations from their text, allowing the same artwork to display content in different languages without creating separate images for each translation. The illustrations are generated through code using SVG, providing a flexible and reusable approach to visual storytelling.

Factors considered during development:

Our team considered content accessibility, readability, bilingual consistency, website performance, and user experience. We also implemented checks to ensure that text fits correctly inside comic speech bubbles in both languages. Other important considerations included keeping the website lightweight, supporting reading even without JavaScript, and respecting user privacy by avoiding cookies and tracking systems.
